audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].side said Ekko while win[5] said Aurelion Sol, and phases[6].side said Skill while win[6] said Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: Two layers rendering different answers for the same row. The content layer matches phases[5].why, which already describes the curve bending, and a 48.98% win rate over 541 games fits Ekko owning levels 1-6.
audit.corrected: Both full-layer sides set to Aurelion Sol to match the content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] called Chronobreak an all-in with 'almost no downside', and spikes[2] named Shadowflame/Stormsurge as the first item while report[8] builds Rod of Ages.
audit.why: Chronobreak is 110 seconds at rank 1. Calling a 110-second ultimate consequence-free teaches the player to fear the wrong window; the truth is the opposite — the two minutes after he spends it are the lane.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[1] around the 110s cooldown and spikes[2] around Rod of Ages plus anti-heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Parallel Convergence was described as a zone that stuns you when you stand in it. Chronobreak's untargetability was never mentioned, nor was the fact that it heals off damage received.
audit.why: Riot's text: the anomaly slows on its own, but it stuns only IF EKKO ENTERS IT. His step-in is the tell, and it is the difference between dodging a zone and dodging a champion. Chronobreak makes him untargetable during the rewind, so damage or a Falling Star spent into it is wasted, and it heals a percentage of damage received — which is what makes Grievous Wounds matter here.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, wants.foe[0] and report[8].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flagged zero cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in this matchup, and sequencingCues was 0.
audit.why: Every 'commit on its cooldown' line named no number, so the reader had nothing to count.
audit.corrected: Chronobreak's 110s at rank 1 and Phase Dive's 325 range written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, spikes[1] and dontsFull[0].d.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Chronobreak' — it is Ekko's real R name. False positive.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Astral Flight like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 and untargetable on the way out — hold your last damage and your R until he lands, then finish him. - Parallel Convergence only stuns if Ekko walks into his own anomaly; his step-in is the tell. - Guard your W Astral Flight.

edits.before: Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Chronobreak makes him untargetable — burst spent mid-rewind is burst wasted. Hold damage for the arrival point; it is 110s at rank 1.

edits.before: Chronobreak gives him a free reset-and-heal engage window, letting him all-in off Convergence with almost no downside if it goes wrong.
edits.after: Chronobreak rewinds him out and heals off the damage he took, but it is 110s at rank 1 — once he spends it, the next two minutes of lane are yours.

edits.before: He still threatens burst windows off Convergence zones, but your Shadowflame/Stormsurge spike starts out-ranging his Timewinder poke and out-damaging his combo in extended trades.
edits.after: He still threatens burst off a pre-placed Convergence, but Rod of Ages plus anti-heal blunts the Chronobreak rewind, and E's execute clears the wave from outside his 1075-range Timewinder.

edits.before: Chronobreak's reset-safety makes his all-in threat spike hardest at level 6
edits.after: Chronobreak undoes a failed all-in and heals him off the damage you dealt

edits.before: Zone you with pre-placed Parallel Convergence for a guaranteed stun setup
edits.after: Pre-place Parallel Convergence, then walk into it himself to stun you

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by making him spend Chronobreak: bait the all-in, fly out with W, and for the next 110 seconds he is a squishy with a 325-range dash.

edits.before: That’s Ekko’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Phase Dive is 325 range — inside it his auto reset lands before your beam.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Rod of Ages rush (or Seraph's), then Archangel's, Liandry's, Rabadon's. Zhonya's vs dive comps. Never skip the mana battery.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Rod of Ages rush (or Seraph's), then Archangel's, Liandry's, Rabadon's. Zhonya's vs dive comps. Anti-heal cuts the Chronobreak rewind.

notes: Parallel Convergence carries both a 'hardCC' and a 'shield' flag; Riot's text confirms both apply only when Ekko himself enters the anomaly, so I wrote the step-in as the tell rather than the placement. The autoreset-burst-tell interaction (Phase Dive charging an empowered attack that then teleports him) is now referenced in dontsFull[0].d but there is no field left with room to explain the wind-up properly — worth a dedicated dosFull entry if the counts ever allow one.
